subject: A session whose output is not a findings bundle has no state that fits
recordedOccasion: from this session's own state after four revisions of work.
severity: low, and it misleads the one reader it is written for. `docs/sessions/INDEX.md` is what an owner scans to see who is doing what, and it currently shows a session that produced two architecture records and a decision as indistinguishable from one created a minute ago.
scope: session management. The fix lands in `docs/legend.md` and the sessions index.

members.statement: Session state derives only from owned bundles, so a session that contributes and designs but owns nothing stays `available`
The sessions index shows such a session as empty, next to sessions holding thirty findings
members.sectionHeading: F2 — the index shows the work as absent

members.statement: Every load-bearing permission is keyed on session identity and nothing can enforce one, because a session cannot declare who it is to anything but a human reading a `metadata.md`
members.sectionHeading: F3 — a session cannot say who it is to anything but a reader

members.statement: The guard written to stop a session writing in the owner's checkout matches on tool name, so a bridged session is invisible to it and it has never fired
members.sectionHeading: F4 — the guard written to stop a session writing in the checkout has never once fired on this session

members.statement: A session's state is stored in `metadata.json` and in the index and they disagree, because `handoff` is declared and cannot be recomputed
members.sectionHeading: F5 — a session's state is stored in two places and they disagree

contributions.contribution: Recorded F4 and F5 — F3's cost measured on a live guard, and a session state stored in two places that disagree

edges.why: the architecture record's account of a session is what a session state has to satisfy; settling one narrows the other
